basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 4.' and it opens 'Vers. 4. Nequaquam moriemini. Dolose hortatur diabolus hominem ad contemptum praecepti'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 4. Nequaquam moriemini. Dolose hortatur diabolus hominem ad contemptum praecepti Dei, ut nollet subdi Deo, sed magis suae esse potestatis.
